headline: Soggy Fenway Sweep Leaves Red Sox Searching For Answers After Bullpen Meltdown
morning_brew: A soggy afternoon at Fenway Park ended in total disappointment as the Red Sox got swept by the Twins in a six to five defeat. Sonny Gray started on the mound but lasted only four innings, giving up three runs on six hits before the bullpen was forced to take over. The relief crew once again failed to hold a lead when the pressure was turned up. Tyron Guerrero picked up the loss after giving up two runs in less than an inning of work, and Garrett Whitlock was charged with a blown save. We fought back with a run in the final frame, but it was too little, too late.

We are now twenty-two and thirty on the year, and the frustration is mounting. We've been here before, we'll be here again, watching a promising stretch get completely wiped out by a bad weekend. Willson Contreras did his part with two hits, including a home run and two RBIs, and Wilyer Abreu added two hits of his own, but you cannot win games when your pitching staff gives up six runs on soggy turf. Atlanta is coming to town next, and if we do not turn this around quickly, this season is going to slip away before June even arrives.

Drake Maye heading into his second year with Josh McDaniels running the offense is the biggest storyline of the football offseason. Maye showed flashes of brilliance during his rookie campaign, but he needs to take a massive leap if this team wants to escape the cellar of the AFC East. Offseason workouts are fine, but the real test will be how McDaniels designs this system to protect the young quarterback and maximize his talent. We need to see progress from day one of training camp.

news_digest.headline: Will Pats QB Drake Maye improve in second year with McDaniels?
news_digest.dans_take: Everything depends on McDaniels building a system that keeps our young quarterback clean.
